morningChecklist: Scan the national weather overview first to orient to the broad synoptic and fire-weather pattern.
Check official Environment Canada warnings and statements for any active hazard signals.
Review CIFFC and CWFIS for the national wildfire picture before drilling into any province or territory.
Skim recent news for evacuations, smoke impacts, notable new fires, and major public messaging changes.

sources.label: GOES IR composite
sources.description: Configured GOES IR loop showing roughly the last 6 hours at a moderately faster animation speed.
sources.why: Fast first-look satellite view for Canada and surrounding upstream weather, pre-tuned for morning scanning.

sources.label: AniMet — RDPA, alerts, lightning, current conditions
sources.description: AniMet blend of 24-hour precipitation, current conditions, alerts, lightning density, and met notes.
sources.why: Excellent all-in-one operational overview for active weather and fire-weather context.

sources.label: AniMet — 500 hPa height, thickness, 3h precip
sources.description: AniMet synoptic setup with 500 hPa height, 1000–500 hPa thickness, and 3-hour precipitation.
sources.why: Useful for quickly interpreting the larger-scale pattern driving Canadian fire weather.

sources.label: AniMet — total column PM2.5
sources.description: AniMet smoke plume view using total column PM2.5 from RAQDPS wildfire smoke products.
sources.why: Adds a fast smoke-transport perspective to the national morning briefing.

sources.label: Environment Canada — weather homepage
sources.description: Environment Canada weather homepage with alerts, forecasts, and national access points.
sources.why: Reliable national entry point for hazard checks and follow-up navigation.

sources.label: CIFFC — active fires map

sources.label: CIFFC — current fires summary

sources.label: CIFFC — situation reports
